title: SAP S/4HANA released CDS views, order to cash: sales documents and sales orders, deliveries, billing documents (I_SalesDocument, I_SalesDocumentItem, I_BillingDocument, ...)
status_note: Proposed, not tested on a customer. Every view, key, association and amount below is taken from public documentation and written in our own words; none of it has been checked against an SAP system by this project, and where a page could not be opened the source says so. validate_plan checks it against your rows. A pack is a sourced suggestion, not proof.

tables.name: I_SALES_DOCUMENT

corresponds_to.note: One row per VBAK row: orders, quotations, contracts and returns; SDDocumentCategory (VBTYP) and SalesDocumentType (AUART) tell them apart. The view has no client field.

tables.note: TotalNetAmount is the net value of the whole document (VBAK.NETWR): summed over a join with the items it counts once per item.

tables.name: I_SALES_DOCUMENT_ITEM
tables.note: The material is the field Material; newer releases also carry the same value as Product. The pack links whichever is there.

tables.name: I_SALES_DOCUMENT_SCHEDULE_LINE
tables.note: Several schedule lines per item: a join of items and schedule lines repeats the item's NetAmount once per schedule line.

corresponds_to.note: The VBAK rows that are sales orders (document category C) only; SalesOrder is VBELN. The same rows as I_SalesDocument restricted to orders.
The VBAP rows of sales orders only.
One row per LIKP row, outbound and inbound deliveries alike.
One row per VBRK row: invoices, credit memos and cancellations; BillingDocumentType (FKART) and BillingDocumentIsCancelled decide whether to count them.
One row per VBRP row. Unlike VBRP, the view carries the currency of its amounts itself (TransactionCurrency).

relationships.condition: Every sales order is a sales document with the same number: the two views read the same VBAK rows. Land one of them, or never add their amounts together.
Every sales order item is a sales document item with the same number: the two views read the same VBAP rows.

ReferenceSDDocument/ReferenceSDDocumentItem name the reference document (LIPS.VGBEL/VGPOS); for deliveries created from sales orders that is the order item. Deliveries without an order reference leave them empty.
SalesDocument/SalesDocumentItem name the sales document item the billing item comes from (VBRP.AUBEL/AUPOS); billing items without a sales document leave them empty.
Only for delivery-related billing; for order-related billing ReferenceSDDocument/ReferenceSDDocumentItem (VBRP.VGBEL/VGPOS) name the order item instead.

traps.title: A CDS view has no client column
traps.text: The tables behind the views start their key with the client (MANDT); a CDS view handles the client itself and does not list it as a field, so I_SalesDocument's key is SalesDocument alone. An extraction of a view therefore holds the rows of one client, the one it was read in. If a landing unions several clients or systems into one table, SalesDocument alone is no longer unique: the key check (validate_plan) shows it, and the landing needs a client or system column of its own in every key and join.

traps.title: TotalNetAmount is the header's, NetAmount the item's
traps.text: I_SalesDocument.TotalNetAmount and I_BillingDocument.TotalNetAmount are the net value of the whole document; I_SalesDocumentItem.NetAmount and I_BillingDocumentItem.NetAmount that of one item. Summing TotalNetAmount over a join with the items counts each document once per item (Krusgraph's 'the total that doubles' check, amounts.py). Sum each amount on its own view.

traps.title: Two views over the same rows
traps.text: I_SalesOrder and I_SalesDocument read the same header table (VBAK), I_SalesOrder only the orders; I_SalesOrderItem and I_SalesDocumentItem the same items (VBAP). A lakehouse that lands both, or a view next to the table it reads, holds every order twice: adding their amounts together doubles the total. The pack lists what each view corresponds to (corresponds_to) so a person can see it; it does not join a view to its table.

traps.title: The landed names depend on the route
traps.text: The pack knows a view by its CDS name (I_SalesDocument) and its fields by their CDS names (SalesDocument, SoldToParty), compared without case and underscores, with or without the I_ prefix. A route that lands the technical SQL view name or an extractor's own name instead, or that renames fields, is not recognised: rename the tables and columns to the view's names in the landing (a view is enough), or give the keys and relationships to plan_backend yourself.

traps.title: Not every released view can be extracted
traps.text: A replication flow reads only views that are released and annotated for data extraction, only some of them support delta, and a view without a key can only be loaded in full; a view built for extraction can differ from the I_ view of the same name in its fields. Check in the system which view your route reads, and that its key fields are the ones the pack names (validate_plan checks the key on the rows).
